name: Report-inspired P2P diagnostic candidates
description: Opt-in canonical activity template; explicit mapping required. Draft screens, not approved obligations. Optional validated automation metric requires additional attributes.

rp_any_commercial_correction.expectation: One affected case if either change occurs; multiple changes still count as one affected case. Raw event counts remain separate.
rp_any_commercial_correction.meaning_when_missed: Reported event occurrence does not establish an avoidable defect.
what_to_check_first: Old/new values, correction reasons, contract version, legitimate amendment review

rp_repeated_quantity_correction.expectation: max(count − 1, 0), saturated at 1; flags at least two recorded changes per item.
rp_repeated_quantity_correction.meaning_when_missed: Reported event occurrence does not establish an avoidable defect.
what_to_check_first: Old/new values, correction reasons, contract version, legitimate amendment review

rp_repeated_price_correction.meaning_when_missed: Reported event occurrence does not establish an avoidable defect.
what_to_check_first: Old/new values, correction reasons, contract version, legitimate amendment review

rp_quantity_change_after_receipt.expectation: Any quantity change at a strictly later timestamp than the earliest goods receipt OR service entry; missing anchor is unmeasured. Equal timestamps do not count.
rp_quantity_change_after_receipt.meaning_when_missed: Not cycle-matched. Partial delivery and services may justify changes; no causal delay or labor estimate.
what_to_check_first: Old/new values, correction reasons, contract version, legitimate amendment review
Service, recurring and installment applicability; handling time if effort is assessed
source: Rząd, Wojnecka, Rutkowski and Guliński (PwC), Investigating Purchase-to-Pay process using Process Mining in a multinational corporation (2019), p.17 (supplied merged collection p.63).

rp_price_change_after_invoice.expectation: Any price change strictly after the first invoice recording; missing anchor is unmeasured, ties excluded.
rp_price_change_after_invoice.meaning_when_missed: Reported event occurrence does not establish an avoidable defect.
what_to_check_first: Old/new values, correction reasons, contract version, legitimate amendment review

rp_invoice_capture_interval.plain_name: Vendor creation to invoice recording interval
rp_invoice_capture_interval.expectation: Calendar days from the sole vendor-invoice event to the sole receipt recording. Reversed endpoints are unmeasured, zero lag is measured. Requires exactly one event of each kind.
rp_invoice_capture_interval.meaning_when_missed: Vendor creation is not AP arrival. Does not measure AP queue, labor or recoverable delay. Repeated, missing and reversed endpoints are outside finite lag coverage; no FIFO matching.
what_to_check_first: Actual invoice arrival/channel, readiness/holds, unique invoice identity
Open invoices and cutoff; business threshold review
source: Porter et al. (CKM Analytix), Balancing Efficiency and Risk in Procure to Pay: Safely Realizing Cost Savings Using Process Mining Techniques (2019), p.14, Table 5 (supplied merged collection p.353); first cycles of completed cases.

rp_invoice_recorded_before_vendor_date.plain_name: Invoice recording before vendor creation date
rp_invoice_recorded_before_vendor_date.expectation: Counts invoice recordings strictly before the vendor creation timestamp in single-event pairs; timestamp ties are allowed.
rp_invoice_recorded_before_vendor_date.meaning_when_missed: Chronology/data-quality review only, not proof of incorrect accounting.
what_to_check_first: Timestamp semantics, business-effective versus posting date, timezone, document identity
source: Porter et al. (CKM Analytix), Balancing Efficiency and Risk in Procure to Pay: Safely Realizing Cost Savings Using Process Mining Techniques (2019), p.14, Table 5 (supplied merged collection p.353); first cycles of completed cases.

rp_invoice_before_order.expectation: Any vendor invoice timestamp strictly before first PO-item creation; both endpoints required. This is not an exact starts-with-vendor cohort.
rp_invoice_before_order.meaning_when_missed: Does not establish unauthorized purchasing; missing authorization logging is not absence of approval.
what_to_check_first: Actual commitment/authorization, framework coverage, emergency exception and posting dates
source: Rząd, Wojnecka, Rutkowski and Guliński (PwC), Investigating Purchase-to-Pay process using Process Mining in a multinational corporation (2019), pp.14–15 (supplied merged collection pp.60–61); reported starts-with cohort, with 3,416 versus appendix 3,415 discrepancy.

rp_recorded_invoice_to_clearing_interval.expectation: Calendar days from sole recorded invoice receipt to sole clearing; reversed endpoints unmeasured. Start is recorded receipt only, never vendor creation.
rp_recorded_invoice_to_clearing_interval.meaning_when_missed: No FIFO pairing, no due-date or payment completion claim. Repeated/missing/reversed endpoints outside finite coverage.
what_to_check_first: Invoice identity, terms/baseline/due date, readiness, block history, actual bank settlement
source: Augusto, Leno and Reissner, BPI Challenge 2019 Report: a Purchase-to-Pay Process Analysis (2019), p.15, Table 7 (supplied merged collection p.175).
Porter et al. (CKM Analytix), Balancing Efficiency and Risk in Procure to Pay: Safely Realizing Cost Savings Using Process Mining Techniques (2019), pp.16–19 (supplied merged collection pp.355–358).

rp_repeated_clearing_limited_receipts.plain_name: Repeated clearing with at most one receipt
rp_repeated_clearing_limited_receipts.expectation: At least two clearing events in a case with zero or one invoice-receipt recording. Includes non-adjacent repeats; NOT the exact report direct-repeat cohort.
rp_repeated_clearing_limited_receipts.meaning_when_missed: Broader repetition screen, never duplicate-payment proof. Exact adjacency is an explicit unsupported constraint gap.
what_to_check_first: Invoice/clearing/payment IDs, allocation and signed reversal links, extraction deduplication review
source: Augusto, Leno and Reissner, BPI Challenge 2019 Report: a Purchase-to-Pay Process Analysis (2019), pp.22–23 (supplied merged collection pp.182–183).
Bekker and Kisjes, Ninth International Business Process Intelligence Challenge — Submission in the Non-Student Category (2019), p.17, Fig.24 (supplied merged collection p.331).

rp_clearing_after_cancellation.expectation: Any clearing at a strictly later timestamp than first invoice cancellation. Missing cancellation is unmeasured; ties excluded.
rp_clearing_after_cancellation.meaning_when_missed: No document or cycle matching, no immediate-adjacency claim, no proof of payment after a void invoice.
what_to_check_first: Cancellation document identity, replacement invoices, clearing allocation, signed reversals, payment records
source: Augusto, Leno and Reissner, BPI Challenge 2019 Report: a Purchase-to-Pay Process Analysis (2019), pp.22–23 (supplied merged collection pp.182–183).
Bekker and Kisjes, Ninth International Business Process Intelligence Challenge — Submission in the Non-Student Category (2019), p.17, Fig.24 (supplied merged collection p.331).

rp_clearing_without_recorded_invoice.expectation: Cases with no invoice-receipt event and one or more clearing events; denominator is invoice-bearing cases lacking receipt.
rp_clearing_without_recorded_invoice.meaning_when_missed: Missing event may reflect logging. Does not establish settlement without an invoice obligation.
what_to_check_first: Invoice linkage, extraction coverage, alternate settlement and credit processes
source: Augusto, Leno and Reissner, BPI Challenge 2019 Report: a Purchase-to-Pay Process Analysis (2019), pp.22–23 (supplied merged collection pp.182–183).
Bekker and Kisjes, Ninth International Business Process Intelligence Challenge — Submission in the Non-Student Category (2019), p.17, Fig.24 (supplied merged collection p.331).

rp_recorded_transfer_failure.expectation: At least one explicit transfer-failure event among cases with transfer or failure evidence; no actor identity classification.
rp_recorded_transfer_failure.meaning_when_missed: Explicit interface failure evidence only. Does not establish automated execution mode, labor or general automation opportunity; report provides the question, not this exact operational rule.
what_to_check_first: Interface/automation configuration, failure reason, retry outcome, eligibility and recovery effort
source: Porter et al. (CKM Analytix), Balancing Efficiency and Risk in Procure to Pay: Safely Realizing Cost Savings Using Process Mining Techniques (2019), pp.10–13 (supplied merged collection pp.349–352).
Hüser and Heisenberger, BPI Challenge 2019 (2019), pp.19–20 (supplied merged collection pp.251–252).

rp_validated_automation_recovery.expectation: Recovery count > 0 only for eligible cases with validated execution evidence. Missing metric remains unmeasured; no regex on user IDs.
rp_validated_automation_recovery.meaning_when_missed: Optional component omitted when required validated fields are unavailable. No labor estimate from identity or event count.
what_to_check_first: Mapped validated eligibility, validated execution evidence and numeric recovery count
Rule/configuration version, measured handling minutes and errors
source: Porter et al. (CKM Analytix), Balancing Efficiency and Risk in Procure to Pay: Safely Realizing Cost Savings Using Process Mining Techniques (2019), pp.10–13 (supplied merged collection pp.349–352).
Hüser and Heisenberger, BPI Challenge 2019 (2019), pp.19–20 (supplied merged collection pp.251–252).

constraints.description: Price or quantity correction observed. One affected case if either change occurs; multiple changes still count as one affected case. Raw event counts remain separate.
Repeated quantity corrections. max(count − 1, 0), saturated at 1; flags at least two recorded changes per item.
Repeated price corrections. max(count − 1, 0), saturated at 1; flags at least two recorded changes per item.
Quantity change after first receipt. Any quantity change at a strictly later timestamp than the earliest goods receipt OR service entry; missing anchor is unmeasured. Equal timestamps do not count.
Price change after invoice recording. Any price change strictly after the first invoice recording; missing anchor is unmeasured, ties excluded.

Vendor creation to invoice recording interval. Calendar days from the sole vendor-invoice event to the sole receipt recording. Reversed endpoints are unmeasured, zero lag is measured. Requires exactly one event of each kind.
Invoice recording before vendor creation date. Counts invoice recordings strictly before the vendor creation timestamp in single-event pairs; timestamp ties are allowed.
Vendor invoice before order creation. Any vendor invoice timestamp strictly before first PO-item creation; both endpoints required. This is not an exact starts-with-vendor cohort.
Invoice recording to clearing interval. Calendar days from sole recorded invoice receipt to sole clearing; reversed endpoints unmeasured. Start is recorded receipt only, never vendor creation.

Repeated clearing with at most one receipt. At least two clearing events in a case with zero or one invoice-receipt recording. Includes non-adjacent repeats; NOT the exact report direct-repeat cohort.
Clearing after invoice cancellation. Any clearing at a strictly later timestamp than first invoice cancellation. Missing cancellation is unmeasured; ties excluded.
Clearing without recorded invoice receipt. Cases with no invoice-receipt event and one or more clearing events; denominator is invoice-bearing cases lacking receipt.
Recorded transfer failure. At least one explicit transfer-failure event among cases with transfer or failure evidence; no actor identity classification.
Validated automation recovery evidence. Recovery count > 0 only for eligible cases with validated execution evidence. Missing metric remains unmeasured; no regex on user IDs.
